bridgeRouteRisk.summary: JUSD's canonical native issuance is on Polygon, while the BSC deployment is a Chainport BridgeMintableToken representation. The BSC destination can be minted by Chainport bridge infrastructure and governed through Chainport Congress, so durable BSC supply carries external lock/mint exposure; the token-level mint is unbounded even though generic Chainport documentation describes source-side conservation.

protocols.name: Chainport
protocols.note: Chainport's wrapped-asset documentation describes a lock-source / mint-target / burn-before-return model; current statistics list JUSD as ported across two chains.

routes.reviewNote: At BSC block 116345894 (2026-08-16 21:39:37 UTC), the JUSD destination proxy resolved to BridgeMintableTokenV2 implementation 0x877d233c59741f36154bb7fbaea853e317fbdcd6. Its classified bridge authority can mint arbitrary amounts at the token level, while Chainport Congress can replace the authority and proxy implementations. Generic Chainport documentation describes source-side lock/burn conservation, but the JUSD-specific source vault, remote identifier, validator/signing policy, rate limits, and burn reconciliation remain unresolved; this route is therefore reviewed as external lock/mint rather than treated as proven conserved supply.

routeChecks.rateLimits: The verified BridgeMintableTokenV2 mint path has no aggregate or per-call amount ceiling; the current Chainport bridge implementation is unverified, so JUSD-specific route limits cannot be verified.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: At the observation block, the destination token's chainportBridge was 0x5c80ae9c3396ca4394f9d8e6786ed9aa74489afe and its classified authority can mint and pause. Congress-only setters can replace the bridge and Congress addresses.

bypassSurfaces: Token-level classified-authority minting is not bounded by a source-lock proof in the destination implementation.
controls.evidence: At BSC block 116345894, a simulated one-token mint reached the destination token's mint path from the live chainportBridge address 0x5c80ae9c3396ca4394f9d8e6786ed9aa74489afe and from Chainport Congress 0xb6b4c7ac240b1f176c5589d064733066a83884a1. The token's chainportBridge and chainportCongress are the two classified authorities for mint and pause; the token source applies no aggregate or per-call mint ceiling. The generic Chainport route may intend source-side conservation, but the JUSD-specific lockbox, remote route, validator/signing policy, rate limits, and burn reconciliation are not verified.

controls.label: JUSD BSC Chainport Congress
controls.capDescription: The custom Chainport Congress uses a quorum of 3 from four members to propose and execute arbitrary target calls, including bridge authority, proxy-admin, peer, and pause changes. The verified execute path has no mandatory execution timelock; its three-day delay is only the cancellation window for proposals below quorum.

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: Congress-only setters can replace the destination token's chainportBridge and chainportCongress addresses; the JUSD-specific remote route identifier is not verified.
routeChecks.rateLimits: No JUSD-specific Chainport rate-limit policy was identified in the reviewed sources.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The verified Congress execute path permits arbitrary target calls after the members-registry quorum and has no mandatory execution timelock; the three-day delay is only a cancellation window for below-quorum proposals.

bypassSurfaces: The Congress can execute arbitrary target calls after quorum, including calls that replace bridge authorities or mint-critical proxy implementations.
